questions.q: What is a depreciation calendar made up of?
options: A list of asset categories
A sequence of fiscal years broken into periods, almost always monthly
A list of employees who can approve asset additions
A single fixed depreciation rate
questions.explain: The depreciation calendar structures a book's time dimension into fiscal years and periods, almost always monthly, for calculating and allocating depreciation.

questions.q: What does "current open period" mean for a depreciation book?
options: The period in which the book was first created
The single period depreciation will calculate into if run right now
Any period that has ever been open
The final period of the fiscal year only
questions.explain: At any moment a book has exactly one current open period — everything before it is closed, everything after it hasn't opened yet.

questions.q: Can a depreciation period generally be reopened once it has been closed?
options: Yes, at any time with no restrictions
No, the depreciation calendar generally only moves forward
Only on the last day of the fiscal year
Only if the asset was added that same period
questions.explain: Like GL period close, once a depreciation period is closed it generally cannot be reopened — the calendar moves forward only.

questions.q: How are mistakes discovered after a period has closed typically corrected?
options: By reopening the closed period directly
By deleting the asset and re-adding it
With a correcting transaction dated into the current open period
They cannot be corrected at all
questions.explain: Since closed periods generally can't be reopened, corrections are made with a transaction (such as a cost adjustment) dated into the current open period.

questions.q: Why do many implementations align the depreciation calendar's period naming with the GL calendar even though the two are technically independent structures?
options: Oracle Fusion requires them to use identical names
It makes later reconciliation between Assets and GL easier
It is required for depreciation to calculate at all
It prevents tax books from being created
questions.explain: Aligning period naming conventions between the depreciation calendar and the GL calendar simplifies reconciliation work later, even though the calendars are independent structures.
